body:
`flatten()`, `unflatten()` and `diff()` spent most of their time on work that can be avoided: searching a `std::map` from the root for every flattened path, splitting every key into a vector of strings and walking it from the root again, and building every diff operation from initializer lists. This makes them 1.4× to 2.3× as fast, and `patch()` a little faster. Output, exceptions and the state left after a failing patch are unchanged.

One commit per change:

1. **flatten:** for object types with `emplace_hint` (`std::map`), each path is inserted next to the entry added last, since paths come out in nearly sorted order. `ordered_map` keeps its append without lookup; other object types keep `operator[]`. Path segments are appended in place.
2. **unflatten:** keys are checked by a scan that throws the same `parse_error.107`/`108` as `split()`, skipping the part shared with the previous key. The prefixes that become arrays are kept in a small hash set of key slices instead of a prefix tree, and the walk keeps the values along the previous key's path, so only the part of a key that differs from the previous one is looked up. The array/object decision is unchanged.
3. **patch:** `add`, `remove`, `replace` and `test` on a path without escapes that denotes existing values (as `diff()` creates them) are applied without building a `json_pointer`. Everything else, and every operation that would fail, takes the existing code.
4. **diff:** operations are built member by member instead of from initializer lists (about 25 allocations each before), and paths are built in place.
5. **diff:** objects with the same keys in the same order are walked together without lookups, and the path is one buffer that is extended and shortened again.

## Performance

`tests/benchmarks` of #5845, Apple M1 Max, Apple Clang 21, `-O3 -flto`, C++11, medians of 4 interleaved rounds against `develop` (5683f5e02):

| benchmark | develop | this PR | speedup |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| `Flatten/canada` | 22.09 ms | 11.67 ms | 1.89× |
| `Flatten/citm_catalog` | 4.84 ms | 3.03 ms | 1.60× |
| `Flatten/twitter` | 2.87 ms | 2.03 ms | 1.41× |
| `FlattenOrdered/citm_catalog` | 2.37 ms | 2.22 ms | 1.07× |
| `FlattenOrdered/twitter` | 1.49 ms | 1.42 ms | 1.05× |
| `Unflatten/canada` | 33.34 ms | 15.61 ms | 2.14× |
| `Unflatten/citm_catalog` | 8.27 ms | 3.68 ms | 2.25× |
| `Unflatten/twitter` | 4.38 ms | 2.25 ms | 1.94× |
| `Diff/canada` | 7.83 ms | 4.02 ms | 1.95× |
| `Diff/citm_catalog` | 1.88 ms | 1.25 ms | 1.51× |
| `Diff/twitter` | 1.24 ms | 0.71 ms | 1.75× |
| `Patch/canada` | 5.46 ms | 4.99 ms | 1.10× |
| `Patch/citm_catalog` | 1.85 ms | 1.77 ms | 1.04× |
| `Patch/twitter` | 1.06 ms | 0.98 ms | 1.09× |

`patch()` is bound by the copy of the document it makes (3.4 of 5.5 ms on canada). For `ordered_json`, `unflatten()` is 2.05× to 2.2× and `diff()` 1.65× to 1.85× as fast; `patch()` 1.03× to 1.09×.

## Breaking changes

None. Only private and `detail` code changes; the public API, the output and the exceptions are unchanged. The private helpers `json_pointer::prefix_tree` and `json_pointer::get_and_create` are removed, and `basic_json::diff_recursively`/`diff_unequal` take the path as a mutable buffer; none of them is part of the public API.

## Testing

- A differential check against `develop` on canada, citm_catalog and twitter, for `json` and `ordered_json`: `flatten()`, `unflatten()`, `diff()` at three change densities and `patch()`, plus about 90,000 random flattened objects (valid and invalid keys), 200,000 random patches (including the partially patched state after a failing one) and random diff/patch and flatten/unflatten round trips. 137 MB of output, byte-identical, including exception ids and messages.
- Unit tests: json_pointer, json_patch, ordered_json, ordered_json2, ordered_map, alt-string, custom-array-type, custom-object-type, custom-key-type, diagnostics, diagnostic-positions, merge_patch, merge_diff, same-number-types, readme, throw_messages, regression2, allocator, constructor1, pointer_access, class_const_iterator; json_patch, json_pointer and ordered_json also with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1`.
- Every commit compiles without warnings with GCC 16 and Clang (C++11, `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Wold-style-cast -Werror`), and its `single_include` matches `make amalgamate`.

This PR was written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.
